title: observability-promotion-receipt.v2
description: What a completed promotion proved, recorded as facts a later reader can re-check. The receipt is one of the three artifacts drift compares (AGENTS.md rule 12): desired state in Git, live state read from the APIs, and this record of the last verified deployment.  v2 adds the ADR-0006 halves a receipt needs to be checkable without disclosing anything: the approved plan the promotion executed (issued by the deployment control plane, referenced here), the private inventory it resolved against, and the exact image digests that ran — each by identity and digest, never by value. `host.identity` became `host.target_id` for the same reason. This receipt remains the artifact most likely to be pasted into a ticket, so every field it permits is still a count, a boolean, a digest, a revision, a version string, a logical name or a timestamp.

outcome.description: A receipt is written for a failure too. A promotion that leaves no record is indistinguishable from one that never ran.

authorization.description: The approved deployment plan this promotion executed, as issued by `dotmac-deployment-control`. CONSUMED, NEVER DEFINED HERE: this repository is an adopter of the deployment control plane, not a second one, so it records WHICH approved plan it carried out and owns none of the approval semantics. Re-deriving `plan_digest` is how a reader checks that the promotion executed the plan it claims.

private_inventory.description: The ObserverInventoryV1 document the render resolved against. Its VALUES never appear here (ADR-0004). Version and digest are enough to prove two promotions consumed the same environment, and to report drift without printing an endpoint.

images.description: What actually ran, by digest. Must equal the approved plan's image set: a receipt recording different images from the ones approved is the finding, not a formatting difference. Public — these are upstream images and naming one discloses nothing about this estate.

target_id.description: The LOGICAL host. Its resolved identity is in the private inventory, whose digest this receipt already carries, so a reader with access to both can establish which machine was changed and a reader with neither learns nothing.

previous.description: Null only on the very first promotion. Any later null means the rollback target was not captured, which invalidates rule 11.

rules_healthy.description: AGENTS.md rule 10. Counted from rules that EXIST and evaluate cleanly. Absence never counts as health.

delivered.description: Proved at the RECEIVER, not at Alertmanager's outbound attempt. A 200 from a delivery API is not evidence a human can be reached.

document_ref.description: A private document named by identity rather than content. All three fields together: a digest alone cannot say which document was supposed to produce it, and a version alone is a label anyone can reuse.

plan_digest.description: The frozen plan's digest, as issued by the deployment control plane. A plan is frozen at proposal, so this identifies exactly what was approved rather than whatever the desired state happens to say now.

approval_decision_ref.description: An opaque reference to the approval decision, resolvable in the deployment control plane. NOT a person's name. A name typed into an artifact is self-attested — nothing verifies it and the person named is never notified — and a reference resolvable in the system that actually recorded the decision is the only form of this field worth keeping.

approval_policy_code.description: Which approval policy the decision was taken under. Optional here because whether a plan requires approval at all is the control plane's per-plan declaration, never this repository's inference.

plan_ref.description: A reference into `dotmac-deployment-control`'s approved-plan record. The field names mirror that owner's deliberately; if the two ever disagree, the owner is right and this is the defect.

run_ref.description: An immutable external run identifier. Null means the step genuinely did not run, and a reader must treat the corresponding claim as unproven rather than assumed.
